subject: elephant
pitch: A gentle African elephant calf. Wrinkly slate-grey skin with a dusty, reddish tint from rolling in the dirt, huge fan-shaped ears with a pink flush on the inside, a curious trunk curling forward, stubby baby tusks, long lashes over kind brown eyes, a little tufted tail and round, padded feet with pale toenails.
reasoning:
I'm planning out an elephant calf model with a joint hierarchy—spine, neck, head, jaw, trunk, ears, legs, and tail—sized around 1.1m at the shoulder, and setting up the coordinate orientation before building the body loft along the spine.

Now I'm defining the barrel-shaped body, pillar legs positioned at the front and hind, a round head with a trunk chain curling forward and tapering in radius. I'm working out the skeleton structure, starting with a root pelvis joint and a spine chain built from catmull points, making sure the chain's first joint aligns with the pelvis for proper parenting.

Setting up neck and jaw joints...

For skin coloring I'm blending a mottled slate-gray with a reddish dust tone, weighting the dust color heavier toward the lower body for countershading.

Blending the two mottled tones with a smooth vertical falloff plus noise, then adding subtle darker wrinkle lines using a sine pattern for texture. Now moving on to constructing the legs with chained segments and sweep radius for the front left leg.

Each leg uses a three-point catmull path with named joints, tapered radius, and round caps, with a cylinder foot attached at the ankle bone. I'm adding small pale toenail boxes arranged around the front edge of each foot.

I need to assign parents for each limb chain: front legs parent to "spine2", hind legs parent to "pelvis", matching the default spine joint names. Mirroring to the right side just means negating x and appending "R" to names, looping over both sides.

For the head, I'm placing a neck chain running up to a head joint, then building the head shape itself as a scaled sphere, with twin forehead domes positioned slightly apart to mimic an elephant's distinctive double-dome skull, plus a small snout bump at the front — all using low-poly icosahedron geometry for the blocky style.

Now I'm defining the trunk as a five-segment curved chain from the head down and forward, tapering the radius along its length and rounding off the tip, then thinking about adding subtle ring bands along the trunk to suggest wrinkles.

For the trunk tip, I'll add two small dark nostril spheres offset slightly on either side of the trunk end position to give it that detail.

Now I'm adding small ivory tusk cones near the base of the trunk on each side, angled outward and down, using the spike sweep with the head bone, then positioning the eyes on the head sphere's surface at a forward-outward offset.

For the eyes I'm computing where they sit on the sphere's surface using the Pythagorean relation, then layering a brown eye sphere, a darker pupil, and a tiny highlight, with small lash spikes fanning upward and outward from the top of each eye.

Now I'm figuring out the ears as extruded fan shapes attached to the sides of the head, orienting the ear's local plane so it extends outward and back from the attachment point.

I'm sizing the ear proportionally larger for a calf, roughly 0.45m wide, with thin bevel and extrusion for the outer skin shape, then adding a slightly smaller inner extrude for the pink inner surface, figuring out which face direction corresponds to the front versus the body-facing side given how the ear flares backward.

For the pink overlay color I'll use a mottled paint blending dusty pink tones for a natural look, then move on to defining the ear hinge joints with their parent, position, and rotation axis.

Working out the ear outline geometry for mirrored sides, I'm computing the normal vector via cross product of the ear's local x and y axes to get the correct orientation for each ear.

Working out the mirrored normal direction for the pink ear overlay, so the inner offset flips correctly between left and right ears while keeping thickness symmetric...

For the ear tilt and tail shape, I'm placing the ear axis so it droops slightly and sits partly embedded behind the head sphere, then sketching a tail chain of points curving downward from the hip, considering using a catmull-rom spline for smoothness.

For the tail tip, I'm fanning out seven small dark spikes radiating downward and outward to form a tuft, attaching them to the last tail joint, and now sketching a small lower jaw as a sphere beneath the trunk base.

For surface texture, I'm considering scattering tiny bristle spikes across the top of the head using a surface hit-scatter filtered to upward-facing points, skipping the mouth detail for simplicity.

Tweaking leg taper radii...

Checking foot cylinder geometry at the base and refining skin tone shading for lower legs by vertical position. Now I'm working out the eye details—placing a darker flattened eyelid sphere slightly behind a smaller brown eyeball sphere, adjusting their radii and offsets for a convincing layered look.

Verifying the eye placement sits properly on the scaled head sphere surface relative to the snout and trunk attachment point, then moving on to finalize the lathe texture paint and skip adding a mouth detail before wrapping up with metadata and the default export.

Now I'm working out the neck chain as a two-point polyline linking the spine to the head joint, and the spine chain as a catmull curve through the pelvis and two spine points, checking that the body loft's station heights and widths overlap enough with the head sphere so no gaps appear at the neck.

For the hind legs I'll parent them to the pelvis with hip joints offset laterally and slightly back. Now I'm defining small helper functions—one for building position tuples and one for creating sphere "ball" parts with radius, position, scale, color, and bone binding—before moving into writing the actual body code.

Writing paint function...
